newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian tourism clouded by gloomy summer data.
newsitem.headline: Austrian tourism clouded by gloomy summer data.

text.p: Austria's crucial tourism industry is weathering a difficult summer as locals holiday abroad and foreign visitors by-pass the nation's Alpine charms, the Economy Ministry said on Tuesday.
"We fear a significant downturn. Tourism earnings in the 1997 summer season will deteriorate again," the ministry said in a report.
It forecast a summer tourism deficit of around eight billion schillings, down from a one billion schillings surplus in the summer of 1996. That performance was considered catastrophic at the time.
For the full-year the ministry saw Austria's tourism surplus halved to 11.4 billion schillings.
"Despite a few regional bright spots, overall the industry is in quite a serious situation," the ministry said, adding that it did not expect a recovery before 1999.
Overnight stays by foreign visitors fell 5.9 percent to 44 million in the five months to the end of May. Overnight stays by Austrians declined 5.4 percent to 17 million.
The ministry saw full-year sales down four percent in real terms to 176 billion schillings.

Austria's current account deficit, which used to rely on tourism earnings to plug the holes, widened to 11.4 billion schillings in the first quarter of 1997 from 4.6 billion in the same period the previous year.
